title: ee.daemon.stop.v1
description: The data object in the ee.response.v2 envelope from ee daemon stop. The CLI validates endpoint ownership and the daemon protocol, sends a shutdown request, and waits for the daemon to release its workers and socket. It does not unlink an arbitrary supplied path.

socketPath.description: Absolute workspace endpoint targeted for shutdown: `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/ee/d-<workspace-hash>.sock`, or the private per-UID `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ee-${uid}/d-<workspace-hash>.sock` fallback. Long runtime paths use /tmp/ee-${uid}. Matches daemon start's canonical workspace hash; override with --socket.

removed.description: `true` when the socket file existed and `fs::remove_file` succeeded; `false` when the socket file did not exist at call time (idempotent no-op). A failed `fs::remove_file` does not emit this envelope at all — the handler returns a `DomainError::Configuration` instead, which surfaces via the canonical `ee.error.v2` envelope. Multi-agent harnesses can therefore treat any successfully emitted `ee.daemon.stop.v1` envelope as 'socket is now absent', regardless of `removed`.
